steps.title: Four sentences about how things are made.
steps.sub: In none of them do we say who does it.

items.text: They are baked in the oven.
Those first cans were made of iron.

steps.title: Compare the two sentences.
steps.sub: A French chef invented cans in 1810. · Cans were invented in 1810.
options: The second one puts the important thing first and leaves out the doer.
The second one happened later in time than the first one did.
The second one is a question and the first one is a statement.
steps.answer: The second one puts the important thing first and leaves out the doer.
steps.why: Use the passive when the doer is unknown, obvious or simply not the point.

steps.title: The passive
steps.html:
Active — we say whoPassive — we don’t need to
Machines produce cans.Cans are produced by machine.
They bake them in the oven.They are baked in the oven.
A French chef invented cans in 1810.Cans were invented in 1810.
They made the first cans of iron.The first cans were made of iron.
Somebody doesn’t serve it hot.It isn’t served hot.
When did they invent it?When was it invented?

Passive = be + past participle. Present: am / is / are + participle. Past: was / were + participle.

The participle is the third form: make – made – made, produce – produced – produced, eat – ate – eaten.

Add by + the doer only when it is genuinely useful: Cans were invented by a French chef. Most of the time you leave it out.

Common mistake: forgetting be. Say Cans are produced by machine, not Cans produced by machine.

You will meet the passive again in Unit 11, when the news reports what has happened.

steps.prompt: What were the world’s first food containers made from?
steps.answer: Animal skins and large leaves.

steps.title: Listen to part 1: the first containers and the prize.
steps.prompt: Who invented metal cans, and when?
options: A French chef, Monsieur Appert, in 1810.
A British soldier and cook, in 1900.
steps.answer: A French chef, Monsieur Appert, in 1810.

steps.title: Listen to part 1: the first containers and the prize.
steps.prompt: Why did Napoleon offer a prize?
options: To find a way of keeping food safe for soldiers in battle.
To find a lighter metal for the army to carry around.
To design a tin opener that soldiers could use safely.
steps.answer: To find a way of keeping food safe for soldiers in battle.

steps.title: Listen to part 1: the first containers and the prize.
steps.prompt: What were the two problems with the first cans?
options: They were very heavy and almost impossible to open.
They were expensive to make and far too small.
They broke easily and leaked all over the food.
steps.answer: They were very heavy and almost impossible to open.
